# Remove-ZbxProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Removes proxies.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxProxy [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxy>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A proxy collects data for the server from the hosts assigned to it, so a remote site needs only one connection to the server. The Remove-ZbxProxy cmdlet deletes the proxies given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with proxy.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a proxy by name

```powershell
Remove-ZbxProxy -InputObject 'proxy-01' -Confirm:$false
```

-InputObject takes a name, an id or a proxy object. ConfirmImpact is High, so PowerShell asks first unless -Confirm:$false is given.

### Example 2: Delete the proxies a search finds, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' | Remove-ZbxProxy -WhatIf
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' | Remove-ZbxProxy -Confirm:$false
```

Get-ZbxProxy writes proxy objects; Remove-ZbxProxy binds each one and deletes them in one proxy.delete call. Run it with -WhatIf first to see what would go.

### Example 3: Delete a proxy that still monitors hosts

```powershell
$proxy = Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' -SelectHosts
if ($proxy.Hosts) { Set-ZbxHost -InputObject $proxy.Hosts.HostId -MonitoredBy Server | Out-Null }
Remove-ZbxProxy -InputObject $proxy -Confirm:$false
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' | Select-Object HostName, MonitoredBy
```

The API refuses to delete a proxy that monitors hosts, so hand them back to the server first.

The proxy(s) to change or delete: ids, names or objects, from the pipeline or by position. -Id is an alias.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxy>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
